question: Can I use the counseling service, and how do I register?
required_facts: Yes: counseling is available to international students (Seoul OIA program; ERICA program free for all international students)
Seoul: visit the OIA or e-mail, fill in the application form, interview or test, then counseling (phone 02-2220-2450, International Building 218)
ERICA: book through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing
reference_answer: Yes. At Seoul, visit or e-mail the OIA (International Building room 218, 02-2220-2450), fill in the application form and take an interview or test before counseling. At ERICA, the service is free for all international students and you book it in HY-in under Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing.
notes: Campus unstated; booking routes differ, 2 branches (11.6). Visiting status does not change eligibility.

question: Can I live in the dorm and how do I apply?
required_facts: Seoul: new-student dorms are first come first served and only for the first semester of enrollment; apply on the dormitory website with your application number
ERICA: apply in January-February or July-August; new students get priority; submit tuberculosis screening report and passport; apply via HY-in
reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At Seoul, dorms are assigned first come first served and only for your first semester; apply through the dormitory application site with your application number. At ERICA, new students get priority; apply in January-February or July-August through HY-in with your passport and a tuberculosis screening report.
notes: Campus unstated; Seoul and ERICA routes differ (11.6). Seoul evidence is the 2026 fall acceptance guide for new undergraduates.

question: How do I go on leave and then return?
required_facts: ERICA: apply for leave through HY-in with passport/RC upload, not in person; leave Korea within 30 days; return via HY-in only with passport, form and bank balance certificate
Seoul: return (re-registration) is online only (in person or e-mail not accepted) with passport and original bank balance certificate; undergraduate leave is 1 year at a time

inapplicable_evidence.why: graduate leave limits, student is undergraduate

reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At ERICA, apply for leave online in HY-in (not in person), leave Korea within 30 days, and apply for return through HY-in with your passport, the ERICA form and a bank balance certificate. At Seoul, return is called re-registration, is online only, and needs your passport and an original bank balance certificate. Undergraduate leave is one year at a time on both campuses.
notes: Campus unstated; Seoul leave steps are only in notices, return steps differ by campus. Graduate leave rows excluded.

question: Do I need to buy the university insurance?
required_facts: Seoul: enrolled students are insured through the university budget; students who completed coursework pay 25,000 won themselves
ERICA: premium (KRW 25,000) is billed with tuition; returning students or those who completed the course must subscribe individually online
reference_answer: It depends on your campus and status. At ERICA a completed-coursework student subscribes individually through the insurance company website (KRW 25,000); enrolled students pay it with tuition. At Seoul, enrolled students are covered by the university and students who completed coursework pay 25,000 won themselves.
notes: Four distinct answers across campus and academic_status (11.6) so clarify; campus is the best single question.

question: Can I join the short-term outgoing program?
required_facts: Eligibility: ERICA undergraduate students who completed at least 1 semester, cumulative GPA 2.0/4.5 or higher; 8+ enrolled semesters cannot apply
Apply online in HY-in > Application > Credit Exchange Management > Short-term Exchange Program application
reference_answer: The short-term outgoing programs are open to ERICA undergraduates who completed at least one semester with a GPA of 2.0/4.5 or higher, and you apply in HY-in. The page does not mention incoming exchange students, so confirm with the outgoing programs office (031-400-4915) whether you qualify.
notes: Only ERICA pages exist; campus unstated but program is ERICA-only. Incoming exchange students are not named; eligibility passage is gold (9.6).

question: Will the university handle my visa as a group?
required_facts: OIA arranges group applications (announced each semester); check the notices
If you cannot join the group, apply individually at the immigration office (book via HiKorea)
reference_answer: Yes, in most cases. The OIA runs group visa and registration applications each semester, announced in notices. If you cannot join the group, apply individually by booking an appointment on HiKorea and visiting the immigration office.

reference_answer: If you will stay more than 90 days, you must register as an alien within 90 days of entering Korea.
